I want to own a gun. I live in California and have never even so much as held one. Where should I start? Should I buy a gun first or learn to shoot first? Is this a costly hobby? Thanks in advance for any answers!

If you're being serious that you've never held one and would like to start, I'd recommend finding someone in the area that does basic firearm training. There should be TONS near where you live. I just completed an NRA basic pistol shooting class (a requirement in IL to get a concealed carry license). It was really good at covering all of the basics of a firearm, safety, etc and had a shooting portion (though we needed our own firearm but many places will let you rent something or even borrow something rent free). I would not recommend buying anything until you've researched the laws in your state as well as your area and figured out what you want it for. Protection? Sport? Hunting? After you figure out what you want to use it for, you would need to figure out what the best one for YOU is to do that. Many of us that own guns now started when we were younger with BB guns, pellet guns, 22's, etc. As far as cost, depends on the weapon and how often you'll shoot. There are some guns I'd like to own but it would cost quite a lot to go to the range and shoot it regularly. And if I'm not going to shoot it, why bother owning it?

Let's start with what do you want it for?

I'd like it mostly for protection, I live alone and have some safety concerns. I also enjoy hobbies and think shooting a gun would be a great useful skill to have. I'm also just generally concerned about having guns in case anyone tries to eff with the 2A. Any advice on the best guns for a first time female shooter?

The smallest protection gun I would go with is a 9mm. It's the most common pistol caliber (so ammo is cheap and easy to find) and you have a LOT of choices for guns. I'm friends with a few police officers and 100% of them recommend Glock because they are very reliable and I have purchased several since then and I'm very happy with them. If you were to go with a Glock, I'd recommend a Glock 19. It is literally the most popular handgun sold in America. But it is a VERY personal choice on what feels the most comfortable in your hand and you may love it or hate it.

I would go to a large gunshop and tell them what you told me and they'll show you a ton of stuff. No matter what they show you, don't buy during that visit. If there is another good gunshop nearby, I'd go there and do the same thing and don't mention you visited the previous one. You'll get new opinions by new people and they will show you stuff as well. While you're talking to them you'll want to find out about the gun laws. Also ask them about gun classes as well as trying the guns out before you buy.

Fellow Californian here. The first step is to obtain a Firearm Safety Certificate (FSC). I'm order to receive one, you need to take a written test. The test is administers at virtually every gun store. It's largely common sense, but I would review material for it. Once that is obtained, you can legally purchase a firearm (long guns and hand guns). Instead of rushing out to buy a new firearm, I would go to a range that rents guns and shoot a few different ones to see what you like. I would also recommend take a basic firearms safety and handling class. They can really help you from developing bad shooting habits. Once you find a firearm you like, purchase it and wait the 10 days provided you pass the background check. Then you're on your merry way. I would recommend you purchase ammo now. Starting January 2018, you will need to go through a licensed firearms dealer to purchase ammo as opposed to having it shipped to your door. As for the costs, it really depends. If you shoot 9mm/.22 handguns, probably not. If you start to get into the more exotic calibers, yes. Feel free to ask me any other questions!
